usage: This is the standard Modern Standard Arabic phrase for wishing someone a happy birthday. It is used in greeting cards, formal broadcasts, and written messages, though in spoken conversation people often substitute it with local dialect greetings. The phrase itself does not change based on the gender of the recipient because the adjectives modify the masculine noun for holiday.

variants.label: General alternative (to a man)
variants.english: May you be well every year
variants.note: A very common alternative used for birthdays and all major holidays, conjugated here for a male recipient.

variants.label: General alternative (to a woman)
variants.english: May you be well every year
variants.note: The female conjugation of the standard holiday greeting.

variants.label: With direct address (to a male friend)
variants.note: Used to add warmth to the standard, somewhat formal MSA phrase.

responses.english: And may you be well (reply to a man)

examples.arabic: عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ، أَتَمَنَّى لَكَ عُمُراً مَدِيداً.
examples.english: Happy birthday, I wish you a long life.

examples.arabic: اليَوْمُ عِيدُ مِيلَادِ أَخِي، عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ لَهُ!
examples.transliteration: alyawmu 3eedu meelaadi akhee, 3eedu meelaadin sa3eedun lahu!
examples.english: Today is my brother's birthday, happy birthday to him!

examples.arabic: أَرْسَلَتْ لِي بِطَاقَةً مَكْتُوباً عَلَيْهَا عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ.
examples.transliteration: arsalat lee bitaaqatan maktooban 3alayhaa 3eed meelaad sa3eed.
examples.english: She sent me a card with 'Happy birthday' written on it.
